deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost entirely figures. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1983-84 notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines in the real projective plane. My reading of the figures is an interpretation, not certain.

(1) Top two figures. A brown pseudoline D is crossed at a vertex s by a bundle of orange pseudolines; s is a multiple point. D is flanked by two green curves. These look like the two local sheets of the boundary of a tubular neighbourhood (strip) of D. In RP^2 such a neighbourhood is a Möbius band, and its boundary is one circle that double-covers D.
- The two green sheets cross each other exactly at the vertex s. The labels D (top left) / D̄ (top right) / D̄ (bottom left) / D (bottom right) show that the sheet called D passes from one side of the brown line to the other through s. So the one-sidedness (the half-twist of the Möbius band) has been concentrated at the vertex.
- The curved arrows indicate pushing the green sheets onto, or off, the brown line.
- Each crossing of a green sheet with an orange line carries labels a, x, y, z (and u, v, w further left) on one sheet and ā, x̄, ȳ, z̄ on the other. Primed versions a', x', ... sit on the other side of the same green curve. So these mark the cells or points adjacent to the crossings, on both sides.
- The marginal NB reads roughly 'x ≠ x̄ (as also x' ≠ x̄'), but x and x̄ [lie on the same] lines!'. The points on the two sheets lying over the same crossing of D with an orange line are distinct, but they are incident to the same orange pseudolines. This is the basic bookkeeping of the double cover 'boundary of the strip → D'.

(2) Bottom figures. A green line (a sheet, or a single pseudoline) is pushed upward across a multiple vertex of orange lines, drawn as a teepee shape. Arrows and a dashed intermediate position show the motion. Blue and black thick segments mark the small cell or segment that collapses and reappears. The two right-hand pictures show the line above the vertex (black band through the bundle) and below it after passage. This is the elementary move of sweeping a pseudoline across a vertex of multiplicity ν. For ν = 3 it is the usual triangle flip.

(3) Context from neighbouring pages.
- The previous page counts quantities such as n−ν−ν'+1 and 2n−(ν+ν'−1). It also tabulates sign sequences ±1 and ε, with ε = +1 when 'la forme spéciale est du type sommital', and asks 'Comment trouver la valeur de ε ?'. So he is tracking how combinatorial invariants change under such moves.
- The next page tries cutting along D and regluing using strips Δ_D and Δ_{D'}. He notes that the vertex s would disappear ('non ! le sommet s disparaîtrait'), and that around a hole where regluing happens he cannot follow the 'circuits autour d'un trou'.
- So this page sets up the local picture: the double sheet of the strip boundary, with its twist placed at a vertex, and its labelled incidences. This prepares a cut-and-reglue (surgery) construction on pseudoline arrangements and the move of a line across a vertex.
errors: No mathematical error is detectable on this page; it consists of figures and a remark. The reading of the green curves as the boundary of a Möbius-strip neighbourhood is interpretive.

ideas.what: Representing the boundary of a tubular (Möbius) neighbourhood of a pseudoline as two local sheets, with the half-twist localized at a multiple vertex, and labelling the incidences on both sheets (x vs x̄)
ideas.modern_name: Double cover of a pseudoline by the boundary of its Möbius-band neighbourhood; lifting a pseudoline arrangement to the sphere (oriented matroid / great-pseudocircle arrangement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folkman–Lawrence 1978 (topological representation of oriented matroids); Goodman–Pollack, Ringel for pseudoline arrangements

ideas.what: Moving a pseudoline (or one sheet of a strip) across a vertex of multiplicity ν
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip / mutation, generalized to multiple points; sweeping (Ringel's homotopy theorem)

ideas.what: Preparing a cut-along-D-and-reglue surgery on arrangements, done on the next page via strips Δ_D and Δ_{D'}
ideas.modern_name: Surgery / gluing of pseudoline arrangements; arrangements on surfaces with boundary

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a local double-sheet model of the strip around a pseudoline, with labelled incidences on both sheets. This is meant to support a cut-and-reglue operation on pseudoline arrangements. On the following page he admits he cannot follow 'circuits around a hole' after regluing, so the surgery is left unfinished. The page is a fragment of that unfinished programme, not a finished result.
missed.quote: NB x ≠ x̄ (comme x' ≠ x̄') mais x et x̄ ... = droites!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Operations that cut and reglue arrangements along a pseudoline, and arrangements on non-orientable surfaces with holes, are studied only sporadically. Examples are pseudoline arrangements on surfaces and mutation graphs of arrangements. A specialist could check whether his intended surgery corresponds to a known operation on oriented matroids, but nothing on this page is new by itself.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds working figures of standard local moves (a line passing a multiple vertex) and a localized Möbius twist, used as bookkeeping for an unfinished surgery idea. It is interesting as part of Grothendieck's little-known pseudoline programme, but contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The figures carry the content and are not transcribed. The top figure is a brown line crossed at a multiple vertex by orange lines, with two green sheets crossing at that vertex and arrows indicating motion. The bottom figures show a green line swept across a vertex of orange lines (dashed intermediate position, blue and black segments), plus two before/after pictures.

Green-curve labels in the middle figure: D at top left and D̄ at top right; D̄ (followed by a small mark, possibly '+') at bottom left and D at bottom right. The sheet named D thus switches sides through the vertex.
The middle figure's labels near the vertex (around the strip crossing) are only partly legible; letters such as r, s, t appear, possibly barred.
The NB is better read as: 'NB x ≠ x̄ (comme aussi x' ≠ x̄') mais x et x̄ [sur les mêmes] droites!' The middle words are uncertain.
The first label row in the top figure appears to be 'ā  a  x̄ ȳ z̄'. The first symbol may be a doubly marked a rather than a repeated ā.
